blocks.text: Every Dockerfile instruction stacks a ==layer==; ordering them well keeps the **cache** warm, and a ==multi-stage== build ships only the artifact, not the toolchain.

cards.title: Layer
cards.text: One per RUN, COPY, ADD. Read-only, stacked.

cards.title: Multi-Stage
cards.text: Many FROMs; final copies artifacts only.

cards.title: BuildKit
cards.text: Parallel stages, cache and secret mounts.

items: Every ==RUN==, ==COPY== and ==ADD== commits a new layer
Cache **hit** when instruction text and its inputs are unchanged
Deleted files in a later layer still exist in earlier ones
Secret copied then removed is **still** in the image
Invalidation is ==top-down==: one miss rebuilds **every** later instruction
Order least to most changing: base, packages, manifests, install, source
`--no-cache` forces a full rebuild
`docker builder prune` clears the build cache

blocks.note: later RUN rm never shrinks earlier layer

items: `COPY . .` **before** dependency install: every edit reinstalls all
`RUN rm` in a later layer: file still in the earlier layer
Copy a secret, delete it later: still in the image history
`apt-get install` and cleanup in separate RUNs: cache lists stay

blocks.note: final image has no compiler or source

items: Build tools and source stay out: Go images ==~800MB== to ==~15MB==
`docker build --target builder .` stops at a stage; run tests there
BuildKit (default) builds independent stages in **parallel**
`RUN --mount=type=cache` keeps package caches between builds
`RUN --mount=type=secret` reads a secret that never hits a layer
Layer per RUN / COPY / ADD; cache reuses unchanged ones
Order stable first, source last; manifests before install
Chain with `&&` and clean up in the **same** layer
Multi-stage: build big, ship the artifact on a slim base
BuildKit mounts for caches and secrets

blocks.title: Debug a fat image
blocks.text: `docker history myimg` shows each layer's size and command; the big layer usually points to a missing cleanup or a `COPY . .` too early.
A container's writable layer dies with the container, so anything worth keeping must live in a ==volume== or ==bind mount== outside that layer.

items: Writable layer is **ephemeral**: `docker rm` deletes every file written there
Image upgrade = new container = new empty layer; old data gone
Volumes live ==outside the layer== and survive rm, restart, upgrade
Three ways to mount: named volume, bind mount, tmpfs

slides.page_title: Volumes: Named, Bind and tmpfs Mounts

cards.title: Named volume
cards.text: Docker-managed under `/var/lib/docker/volumes`; portable, backed up with docker tools

cards.title: Bind mount
cards.text: Maps a host path into the container; live code in dev

cards.title: tmpfs
cards.text: In-memory only, gone on stop; secrets or scratch

cards.title: Anonymous volume
cards.text: `VOLUME` in Dockerfile or `-v /data` with no name; piles up

lines: # backup a named volume to host

items: Storing the database in the ==container layer==, then `docker rm` or upgrade wipes it
Anonymous volumes pile up; run with `--rm -v` or name them
Bind mount + container root: files on host owned by **root**; match uid with `USER` or `chown`
`docker volume prune` deletes every unused volume; ==check first==, it is data loss

blocks.text: Every container gets its own ==network namespace==; Docker wires those namespaces together with __bridges__, an embedded __DNS__ and iptables port rules.

slides.subtitle: (Named volumes, bind mounts, tmpfs)

slides.page_title: Volumes: Named, Bind and tmpfs Mounts (cont.)

items: First mount of an **empty** named volume ==copies image files== at that path into it
Bind mount ==hides== the image's files at that path; host dir wins
Read-only: `-v config:/etc/app:ro` blocks container writes
`-v` and `--mount` give the same result; `--mount` is explicit key=value
`-v` silently __creates__ a missing host directory; `--mount` errors instead

blocks.note: prune asks once, then unused volumes are gone

items: State goes in a ==named volume==, never the writable layer
Bind mounts for live code in dev; volumes for data in prod
Prefer `--mount` in scripts: explicit, fails loudly on typos
`--driver` plugs in NFS, cloud block storage or other backends
Back up with the alpine tar pattern before `prune` or upgrades

blocks.title: Quick test
blocks.text: Run `docker rm` on your DB container. If you cannot `docker run` a fresh one and see the same rows, the data was in the wrong place.

slides.subtitle: (Named volumes, bind mounts, tmpfs)

items: Each container: own interfaces, IP, routing table and port space
Default bridge `docker0`: private IPs ==172.17.x.x==, internet via **NAT**
Default bridge has no name lookup; containers reach each other by IP only
Two containers can both listen on port 80: separate port spaces
`docker network create appnet`: user-defined bridge with ==name resolution==
Embedded DNS at `127.0.0.11` answers `db` with the container's IP
`-p 8080:80` adds an iptables **DNAT** rule host:8080 to container:80
`-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` binds only on ==localhost== of the host
`-P` publishes every `EXPOSE`d port on a random high host port
On one user-defined network `web` dials `db:5432` on the ==container port==
Published ports are only for the **outside**; peers never need `-p`
`host.docker.internal` = the host (Desktop); Linux needs `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway`
`docker network connect appnet web`: a container can sit on ==several networks==
`docker network ls | inspect appnet | disconnect appnet web`
Using `localhost` to reach another container; that is **your own** loopback
App bound to `127.0.0.1` inside: published port connects, then refused; bind ==0.0.0.0==
Relying on names on the default bridge; only user-defined bridges get DNS
Adding `-p` for container-to-container traffic; it is only for outside

blocks.text: Compose turns a pile of `docker run` commands into ==one YAML file== that starts, wires and stops every service as a unit.

items: Namespace per container: own IP, routes, ports
User-defined bridge + DNS: connect by ==name==
`-p` = DNAT for outsiders; peers use container ports
host = speed, none = isolation, overlay = many hosts

blocks.title: Rule of thumb
blocks.text: Put every service of one app on its own `docker network create` bridge, talk by name on container ports, and publish only the edge port.

cards.title: depends_on
cards.text: Orders startup; healthy only with a healthcheck

items: ==Compose== = one YAML, many services, managed as a unit
`docker compose` is the v2 **plugin**; replaces `docker-compose` v1 binary
Top-level keys: `services`, `networks`, `volumes`, `configs`, `secrets`
`version:` key is __obsolete__ and ignored
Project name = directory name or `-p`; prefixes containers, networks, volumes
Service keys: `image`/`build`, `ports`, `environment`, `env_file`, `volumes`, `networks`
Also `depends_on`, `command`, `restart`, `healthcheck`; each service = 1+ containers
Default network `<project>_default`; services resolve by ==service name== (`db:5432`)
`up -d`: builds missing images, creates networks + volumes, starts services
`down`: removes containers + networks; add **-v** to drop volumes too

slides.page_title: Compose: Commands and a web + db Example

blocks.note: condition needs a healthcheck on db
named volume declared at top level

items: `${DB_PASSWORD}` read from the shell or a ==.env== beside the compose file
`${VAR:-default}` supplies a fallback value
`docker-compose.override.yml` merges __automatically__; `-f base.yml -f prod.yml` stacks files
`profiles: [debug]` on a service; starts only with `--profile debug`
`up --scale worker=3` runs replicas; no `container_name`, no fixed host port

slides.page_title: Compose: Commands and a web + db Example (cont.)

items: Expecting `depends_on` to wait for DB **connections**; it only waits for start
Keeping a `version:` key; it is ignored and just warns
`container_name` or fixed host port on a scaled service; replicas collide
Running `down` without `-v`, then wondering why old data persists
Two projects in same-named folders share a prefix; pass `-p`
One YAML; `docker compose up -d` to start, `down -v` for a clean slate
Services talk by ==service name== on `<project>_default`
`depends_on` + `condition: service_healthy` + a `healthcheck`
Override files, `.env` and profiles separate environments
Compose = single host; use an orchestrator for scheduling and self-healing

blocks.title: Started is not ready
blocks.text: Give `db` a `healthcheck` and use `condition: service_healthy`; plain `depends_on` fires the moment the container starts, before Postgres accepts connections.
A ==registry== is where built images live so any host can `docker pull` them; this page covers pushing, pulling, tagging, and keeping the registry clean and safe.

items: `docker login registry.example.com` saves creds in `~/.docker/config.json`
Production: use a ==credential helper==, not plaintext config
Only **changed layers** are transferred; unchanged ones are skipped
Registry ==deduplicates== layers across repositories by digest
`docker run` pulls automatically when the image is missing locally

slides.subtitle: Multi-Container Apps in One File

slides.page_title: Registries: Push, Pull and Tag Strategy

items: ==Registry==: HTTP service that stores and serves image **layers** and **manifests**
==Repository== = one named image (`org/myapp`) holding many tags
{icon:docker} **Docker Hub** is the default public registry when no host is given
Others: {icon:github} `ghcr.io`, {icon:ecr} AWS ECR, {icon:googlecloud} Artifact Registry, Azure ACR, GitLab registry

blocks.note: HTTP registries must be in daemon.json

items: Docker Hub ==rate limits== anonymous and free pulls
CI breaks when limits hit: use a **mirror** or authenticated pulls
Push every image with semver + major + git SHA tags together
Registry stores layers and manifests; repository = name + many tags
Tag then push; the tag names the destination registry
Only changed layers move; digests dedupe across repos
Deploy by digest or semver, never `latest`
Configure cleanup: ECR lifecycle policy or registry GC

blocks.title: Scan and sign
blocks.text: Scan with Docker Scout or Trivy for ==CVEs== before pushing; sign with **cosign** or Docker Content Trust so hosts can verify the image origin.

slides.subtitle: (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR and self-hosted)

slides.page_title: Registries: Push, Pull and Tag Strategy (cont.)

items: `COPY . .` without a `.dockerignore` ships **.env** files and private keys
Deploying `latest`: tag moves, rollback becomes guesswork
Old tags kept forever: set ECR ==lifecycle policies== or run `registry:2` garbage collection
Unscanned, unsigned images pulled straight into production

blocks.text: Containers share the host kernel (page 3), so hardening means ==least privilege== plus hard caps: give the process only what it needs and bound what it can consume.

cards.title: Non-root
cards.text: `USER app`; root inside is root on host if isolation breaks

cards.title: Capabilities
cards.text: `--cap-drop=ALL`, add back only what app needs

cards.title: Limits
cards.text: memory, cpus, pids, log size via cgroups

items: `USER app` in Dockerfile: container root is ==host root== if isolation breaks
**Rootless** mode: daemon runs without root; no privileged ports, slower networking
Never `--privileged` in prod: all capabilities + device access = host root
`--cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE` keeps only the port-80 bind

spec.title: Blast Radius of One App Bug

items: Non-root user, dropped caps, read-only fs by ==default==
Secrets at runtime only; pin and scan images in CI
Always set memory, cpus, pids and log limits
Never `--privileged`, never mount docker.sock in prod

blocks.title: Deny by default
blocks.text: Start from `--cap-drop=ALL --read-only --user app`, then add back only what breaks. The cgroup knobs here are the same ones page 3 explained.
A production-grade container is ==disposable==: one process, an immutable image, state kept outside, and signals that reach the app.
